# Template: layer_stack
A stack of flat slabs seen at an isometric angle, one slab per layer, each named in a column on the right (with an optional one-line note under the name), top layer first. Optionally exploded (gaps between slabs) and with one layer highlighted while the rest turn grey. Choose this scene for requests about layers built on top of each other: a technology or software stack, the OSI / TCP-IP network model, layers of abstraction, the layers of the skin or the atmosphere or the Earth's crust drawn as slabs, a sandwich / laminate / PCB build-up, or "show X as a stack of layers". Not for data (use a bar chart) and not for a nested concentric picture.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "layers": {
   "type": "array",
   "description": "The layers, TOP FIRST (the first item is the top slab). 1–8 layers. Each is a string (the name) or { name, note }.",
   "items": {
    "anyOf": [
     {
      "type": "string"
     },
     {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
       "name": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "Layer name, kept short (≤ 22 characters)."
       },
       "note": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "Optional one-line note drawn smaller under the name (≤ 30 characters)."
       }
      },
      "required": [
       "name"
      ]
     }
    ]
   }
  },
  "highlight": {
   "description": "Optional: one layer to emphasise, by its name or by its index (0 = top). The others are drawn grey.",
   "anyOf": [
    {
     "type": "string"
    },
    {
     "type": "number"
    }
   ]
  },
  "exploded": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Leave a gap between slabs (default true). false stacks them touching, like a solid laminate."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Optional title across the top."
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- layer_<i>: slab i (0 = top), a group of its visible faces — draw these bottom-up (layer_<n-1> first) to build the stack
- layer_<i>_label: slab i's label: a group of the dashed leader, the name (layer_<i>_name) and the note (layer_<i>_note, present only when given)
- title: the title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw the OSI model as a stack of layers." → params: {"title":"The OSI model","layers":[{"name":"7 Application","note":"HTTP, SMTP, DNS"},{"name":"6 Presentation","note":"TLS, encoding"},{"name":"5 Session","note":"sockets, RPC"},{"name":"4 Transport","note":"TCP, UDP"},{"name":"3 Network","note":"IP, routing"},{"name":"2 Data link","note":"Ethernet, MAC"},{"name":"1 Physical","note":"cables, radio"}]}
Request: "Show a typical web app stack and highlight the database layer." → params: {"layers":["Browser UI","API server","Business logic","Database","Operating system"],"highlight":"Database"}
Request: "Draw the layers of the skin as a solid block of three layers." → params: {"title":"Layers of the skin","exploded":false,"layers":[{"name":"Epidermis","note":"outer, waterproof"},{"name":"Dermis","note":"nerves, hair roots"},{"name":"Hypodermis","note":"fat, insulation"}]}
Request: "Show the TCP/IP model and highlight the transport layer." → params: {"title":"The TCP/IP model","highlight":"Transport","layers":[{"name":"Application","note":"HTTP, DNS, SSH"},{"name":"Transport","note":"TCP, UDP"},{"name":"Internet","note":"IPv4, IPv6, ICMP"},{"name":"Link","note":"Ethernet, Wi-Fi"}]}
Request: "Draw the layers of the atmosphere." → params: {"title":"Layers of the atmosphere","layers":[{"name":"Exosphere","note":"700 km and up"},{"name":"Thermosphere","note":"80–700 km"},{"name":"Mesosphere","note":"50–80 km"},{"name":"Stratosphere","note":"12–50 km, ozone"},{"name":"Troposphere","note":"0–12 km, weather"}]}

In YAML: `template: layer_stack` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
